chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: First recording: King Oliver's 1928 date
summary: His first record was King Oliver's date in New York, where Oliver could not play and Louis Metcalf took the trumpet part.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, had you heard King Oliver's band, because they made some first recordings?
The first record I made was for him.
1928 right here in New York but he couldn't play. He had pyorrhea and Louis Metcalf played the trumpet part. That was the first recording ever I made in my life.
If Louis Metcalf played the trumpet, what did King Oliver do?
No, King Oliver couldn't play, he had pyorrhea.
So, actually he didn't make the date.
It was King Oliver's date. It was in his name but he didn't play. Louis Metcalf played.
You mean Metcalf like ghosted for him and said this was King Oliver or did they give Louis Metcalf credit on the record?
Louis Metcalf made it on the record.
But did they give him credit for it, or did they say that was King Oliver?
No, they said it was King Oliver.
Yeah. I've got the record with me.
I have to listen to that.

I'll have to do a whole lot of looking so you let me know by tomorrow. I don't listen to records. My wife she go in the back, and does. ... Sometimes 3 and 4 and 5 o'clock I hear music, pick there clappin her hands and well, she ... playing when the Saints Come Marching In, that's what she's listening to. And, I have quite a collection but I loan them out to people -- stupid. They break them. They Typical either say they forgot to bring them back. They story.
